name: Atomic Dynamic quantization
canonical_description: AtomicChat's AD GGUF layout: the two largest tensor groups get the named precision (ffn_down/ffn_up), allocated with the vendor's own importance matrix and re-measured against the original weights.
mechanism: AD-<ffn_down>-<ffn_up> names what the two largest tensor groups got, collapsed to one name when both match. The importance matrix is collected on the BF16 weights, never on a quant proxy, and each file's KL divergence plus top-1 agreement is measured against the original weights on held-out neutral text with published raw logits for re-measurement.
constraints: Quality rows are vendor-measured on the vendor's held-out text; they do not transfer to other corpora without re-measurement.
The card is a moving target: files are re-quantized and re-measured, so rows need a card pin before exact comparison.
tradeoffs: Smaller AD files trade top-1 agreement for size along a measured curve (e.g. AD-IQ2_XXS 79.44% vs Q8_0 98.92%).
AD naming describes tensor allocation, not a speed claim; speed rows need their own comparison objects.
re_review_triggers: The vendor re-measures the quality table (new KL/top-1).
A setup claims an AD-caused quality or performance effect without a matching comparison object.

canonical_sources.locator: quality table lines 53-70; AD naming lines 72-74; How-we-measured lines 327-351; speed table lines 119-126
canonical_sources.note: Vendor HF card: method, quality rows, and speed rows in one artifact.

note: Canonical technique identity only. A setup-specific claim must still carry its own statement, source, locator, lineage, evidence level, and contrast kind.
